thread:
maria: FYI customer hitting 403 when they set response_format=json + strict=true. They repro locally with curl. Filing here before escalating to eng-runtime.

maria: Repro curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-customer' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -H 'Accept: text/html' 
  -d '{"model":"gptx-3","input":"summarize this","response_format":{"type":"json","strict":true}}'
```

maria: Server returns HTTP 403 with an HTML error page (weird), so the client sees invalid JSON because the body is HTML. Customer says this started after enabling strict mode.

support-bot: Case #CS-48712 created for customer acme-inc. Attached logs + request ids 0x9f3a, 0x9f3b.

akshay: Can you paste the raw response headers from the API call? 403 + HTML smells like our proxy returning an auth or quota page.

maria: Raw response (redacted): 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
X-Request-Id: 0x9f3a
Content-Length: 512

<html>...Access denied...</html>
```

maria: Customer says they were previously using Accept: */* and got JSON back. Only difference was they flipped response_format.strict to true.

josh: Quick notes: when strict=true we validate the model output and downstream pipeline tries to enforce Content-Type negotiation. If downstream proxy sees Accept header that doesn't include application/json it can return an error page instead of returning the generated JSON. Looks like their Accept header is text/html which triggers a fallback page at the edge.

sophie: Are they behind a company proxy that rewrites Accept or injects headers? Also ask them to try Accept: application/json in repro.

maria: Customer tried Accept: application/json and Content-Type: application/json — then API returned 200 and a valid JSON envelope. So workaround is clear, but customer is confused why strict mode flipped this behavior.

akshay: Two hypotheses: (1) strict mode causes the service to set Vary/negotiation headers and our edge checks Accept; (2) an auth proxy (cloud vendor or customer) rewrites Accept when strict flag present (unlikely). I want eng-runtime to look at request->edge routing for request id 0x9f3a to see why Accept was interpreted as text/html.

josh: Adding repro steps for engineering:
- Repro with curl exactly as in thread (note Accept: text/html).
- Observe response headers and body.
- Replay the request in staging with strict=false vs strict=true and compare what our edge returns (particularly any HTML error pages).
- Check edge rules that produce 403 for content negotiation (search for policies that inspect Accept and response_format).

maria: Customer wants a longer-term fix: either (A) when strict=true and the model can produce JSON, we should force the response Content-Type to application/json even if Accept header is permissive, or (B) return a clear JSON error payload instead of an HTML auth page so clients don't break when they expect JSON.

akshay: Agree on (B) — always return machine-friendly error payloads for API paths. Filing eng-runtime follow-up: can we map 0x9f3a -> edge host + rule? @josh can you take point?

josh: Yep, I'm pulling the edge trace now. Will post findings. If we need an immediate customer-facing patch, we can update the doc and add a note in the API error semantics that strict response_format requires Accept: application/json for now.

maria: Thanks — I'll update the support ticket with the workaround and ETA for update. :thumbsup:

josh: Edge trace: the request hit edge-02, policy 'content-negotiation-v1' returned 403 because Accept lacked application/json. Policy change would be needed to prefer response_format param over Accept header. Escalating to eng-runtime with trace id 0x9f3a.

akshay: Great, thanks. After eng-runtime changes, we should run a small canary and add a regression test that simulates proxies rewriting Accept.

maria: Noted. Closing loop once eng confirms.
